make.name: BMW
make.description: German premium car maker. Its electric history runs from the ActiveE trial car and the i3 (2013) to the i4, i5, i7, iX family; from 2025 the 800-volt Neue Klasse models (iX3, i3, iX4) are replacing them, and the iX and i4 are leaving the US market in 2026.

models.name: ActiveE
models.description: Battery-electric conversion of the 1 Series coupe built in Leipzig for BMW's second electric field trial (after the MINI E). About 1,100 were planned, mostly leased for two years to US drivers from January 2012; all were returned to BMW.

generations.name: Field-trial car
generations.description: Lease-only demonstrator; rear motor and 32 kWh pack, the drive layout later used in the i3.

models.name: i3
models.description: BMW's longest-running electric nameplate. It began as the carbon-bodied i3 city hatchback (2013-2022), was reused for a China-only electric 3 Series sedan (2022-2026), and since 2026 names the Neue Klasse electric 3 Series sedan built in Munich.

generations.name: Original (I01)
generations.description: Four-seat carbon-fibre hatchback with rear-hinged rear doors and a rear motor; 60 Ah (22 kWh) pack, upgraded to 94 Ah (33 kWh) for model year 2017. Range-extender (REx) versions are not listed.

generations.name: Facelift (I01 LCI)
generations.description: Restyled bumpers and LED headlights, new sportier i3s; 120 Ah (42.2 kWh) pack from model year 2019. Production ended in mid-2022.

generations.name: China sedan (G28 BEV)
generations.description: Long-wheelbase electric 3 Series sedan built by BMW Brilliance in Shenyang for China only.

generations.name: Neue Klasse (NA0)
generations.description: Electric 3 Series on the 800-volt Neue Klasse platform, unveiled 18 March 2026 and built in Munich from August 2026; China gets a long-wheelbase version.

models.name: i4
models.description: Electric version of the 4 Series Gran Coupe, a five-door liftback built in Munich since 2021. Facelifted in 2024 (M50 renamed M60 xDrive in 2025); BMW says 2026 is its last US model year, with the Neue Klasse i3 sedan taking its place.

generations.name: Original (G26)
generations.description: Launch version with rear-drive eDrive40 and dual-motor M50; smaller-battery eDrive35 added for 2023 and xDrive40 for 2024 in the US.

generations.name: Facelift (G26 LCI)
generations.description: Restyled lights and bumpers, new interior screens; xDrive40 added in Europe. From July 2025 the M50 became the 442 kW M60 xDrive and rear-drive models gained silicon-carbide inverters.

models.name: i5
models.description: Electric version of the eighth-generation 5 Series, built in Dingolfing on the same line as petrol and plug-in models. Sold as a sedan (US and worldwide) and, outside the US, as the i5 Touring wagon; a long-wheelbase eDrive35L is built in China and India.

generations.name: First generation (G60/G61)
generations.description: Launched October 2023 (sedan) and 2024 (Touring); 84.3 kWh pack, up to 205 kW DC. US range rose for model years 2026 and 2027 through efficiency updates.

models.name: i7
models.description: Electric version of the seventh-generation (G70) 7 Series flagship sedan, built in Dingolfing since 2022. The 2027 facelift brought Neue Klasse-derived cylindrical cells (112.5 kWh), 250 kW charging and a NACS port.

generations.name: Original (G70)
generations.description: Launched as the xDrive60; rear-drive eDrive50 and 650 hp M70 added for model year 2024.

generations.name: Facelift (G70 LCI)
generations.description: Production from July 2026: new 112.5 kWh pack with sixth-generation cylindrical cells (about 20% denser), rare-earth-free motors, 250 kW DC and standard NACS port; models renamed 50 xDrive / 60 xDrive.

models.name: iX
models.description: BMW's dedicated electric flagship SUV, built in Dingolfing since 2021 with a carbon-reinforced body. Facelifted for model year 2026 with bigger batteries; BMW ended US sales in 2026 to make room for the iX3 and iX5, but the iX remains on sale in other markets.

generations.name: Original (I20)
generations.description: Launch versions xDrive40 and xDrive50, joined by the 610 hp M60 in 2022.

generations.name: Facelift (I20 LCI)
generations.description: Revealed January 2025: new xDrive45 / xDrive60 / M70 line-up with larger batteries and up to about 30% more range, plus restyled lights and grille.

models.name: iX1
models.description: Electric version of the third-generation (U11) X1 compact SUV, built in Regensburg since 2022 and not sold in the US. A long-wheelbase iX1 is built for China.

generations.name: First generation (U11)
generations.description: Launched as the dual-motor xDrive30; front-drive eDrive20 followed in 2023.

models.name: iX2
models.description: Coupe-styled electric version of the second-generation (U10) X2, built in Regensburg since late 2023. Not sold in the US.

generations.name: First generation (U10)
generations.description: Shares the iX1's drivetrains and 64.8 kWh usable battery.

models.name: iX3
models.description: BMW's compact electric SUV. The first iX3 (G08, 2020-2025) was a rear-drive electric X3 built in Shenyang and never sold in North America; the second (NA5) is the first Neue Klasse model, built in Debrecen from late 2025 and sold in the US from September 2026 as a 2027 model.

generations.name: First generation (G08)
generations.description: Electric X3 with a single 210 kW rear motor and 80 kWh pack; facelifted in 2021. Production in Shenyang ended in 2025.

generations.name: Neue Klasse (NA5)
generations.description: First Neue Klasse model: 800-volt architecture, 108.7 kWh cylindrical-cell pack, 400 kW DC. Global launch as 50 xDrive; China gets a long-wheelbase iX3 L (NA6) with its own drivetrains.

models.name: iX4
models.description: Coupe-SUV sibling of the Neue Klasse iX3 and electric successor to the X4, revealed 8 October 2026 and built in Debrecen. US sales of the 50 xDrive start in March 2027, with the M60 xDrive later in 2027.

generations.name: First generation (NA7)
generations.description: Shares the iX3's 800-volt Neue Klasse platform with a sloping roofline.

models.name: iX5
models.description: First battery-electric X5, part of the fifth-generation (G65) X5 built in Spartanburg from August 2026. It replaces the iX in the US; China gets a long-wheelbase iX5 L.

generations.name: First generation (G65)
generations.description: Launch version 60 xDrive with a 141 kWh (Europe) / 144 kWh (North America) pack and 460 kW DC charging.

models.name: M3 (electric)
models.description: BMW M's first battery-electric car, a four-motor M3 on the Neue Klasse i3 platform (code ZA0). BMW has shown it and confirmed one motor per wheel; power, battery and price were not announced as of November 2026.

generations.name: First generation (ZA0)
generations.description: Quad-motor layout with a clutch that can disconnect the front motors.
